description: High-quality answer criteria for the Project Review Getting Started interview. Employee self-evaluation focused on a specific project rather than broad overall performance.

terms.label: Project Scope, Role & Responsibilities
terms.description: The project, the employee’s role, and the responsibilities or ownership areas assigned.

terms.label: Project Goals, Deliverables & Success Measures
terms.description: The most important project goals, deliverables, timelines, or success measures and how clearly they were understood.

terms.label: Project Results & Impact
terms.description: Results, outcomes, or impact the project produced and the supporting evidence.

terms.label: Execution, Ownership & Follow-Through
terms.description: How the employee managed project responsibilities, followed through on commitments, and responded to changes or obstacles.

terms.label: Work Quality & Project Craft
terms.description: Quality, accuracy, completeness, or professionalism of the project work.

terms.label: Communication, Collaboration & Stakeholder Coordination
terms.description: How communication, collaboration, and stakeholder coordination affected the project.

terms.label: Constraints, Risks & Resource Factors
terms.description: Constraints, risks, dependencies, or resource issues that affected the project and its outcome.

terms.label: Lessons Learned & Future Project Improvements
terms.description: What was learned and what should be repeated, changed, or improved for future projects.

responseProfile.stance: Performance consistently falls materially short of expectations.
Performance has meaningful gaps and requires focused improvement.
Performance reliably fulfills the expectations of the role.
Performance significantly and consistently surpasses expectations.

primaryQuestions.question: What was the project, what was your role, and what responsibilities or ownership areas were assigned to you?
answerGuidance: The project name, project type, or project context being reviewed
Your role/title or functional position during the project
Your assigned responsibilities, ownership areas, decision rights, or deliverables
Which responsibilities you personally owned versus shared with others
Any unclear, changed, or disputed role scope, ownership, or decision rights
How role or scope clarity affected execution, communication, quality, or results
Any temporary, expanded, or informal responsibilities that should be considered

highQualityCriteria.label: Project Review

primaryQuestions.question: What were the most important project goals, deliverables, timelines, or success measures, and how clearly were they understood?

Any measurable targets, acceptance criteria, quality standards, customer outcomes, or stakeholder expectations
How clearly project expectations were communicated or understood
Which goals or deliverables were formally assigned versus implied, evolving, or informal
Any changes to goals, timelines, deliverables, or success measures during the project
How changes affected expectations, prioritization, quality, or outcomes

primaryQuestions.question: What results, outcomes, or impact did the project produce, and what evidence best supports your view?
answerGuidance: The most important project results, outcomes, accomplishments, deliverables, improvements, or contributions
What specifically was achieved, delivered, improved, solved, stabilized, or learned
Why those results mattered to the team, customer, stakeholder, organization, or project objective
How outcomes connect to project goals, priorities, responsibilities, or expected outcomes
Evidence such as metrics, deadlines met, stakeholder feedback, customer outcomes, or operational outcomes
Actions you personally took that contributed to the outcome
Results that exceeded, met, or fell short of expectations, and why
Any constraints, dependencies, resource limits, or scope changes that affected results

How you identified risks, solved problems, asked clarifying questions, or escalated issues
What you controlled directly versus what depended on others, resources, or external conditions

primaryQuestions.question: How would you describe the quality, accuracy, completeness, or professionalism of your project work?

Evidence such as rework, errors, feedback, acceptance, quality checks, testing results, or defect patterns
Any errors, missed details, rework, quality issues, or preventable problems and what caused them
How timeline, scope, review processes, tools, feedback, resources, or dependencies affected quality

primaryQuestions.question: How did communication, collaboration, and stakeholder coordination affect the project?

How project updates, meetings, handoffs, decisions, feedback, documentation, and escalations happened
Communication or collaboration practices that helped project progress, quality, trust, or outcomes
Communication or collaboration issues that caused friction, delay, confusion, missed expectations, rework, risk, or negative outcomes

Improvements to communication, collaboration, meetings, feedback, documentation, or handoffs for future projects

primaryQuestions.question: What constraints, risks, dependencies, or resource issues affected the project, and how did they influence the outcome?
answerGuidance: Constraints, risks, dependencies, resource issues, support needs, context factors, or fairness considerations that affected the project
Examples such as workload, staffing, tools, budget, access, timing, scope change, process, competing priorities, approval delays, or cross-functional dependencies
How those factors affected results, execution, quality, communication, timeline, stakeholder confidence, or learning
Which factors had the greatest effect on the project
Which factors you could address directly versus those requiring manager, team, stakeholder, organizational, vendor, or system support
Whether outcomes or expectations should be interpreted differently because of those factors
Risk management, resource, support, process, sequencing, or prioritization changes for future projects
